options.explanation: This is not the correct statement about the reflection of light.

options.text: The angle of incidence is always less than the angle of reflection
options.explanation: This is not the correct statement about the reflection of light.

options.text: The angle of incidence is always equal to the angle of reflection
options.explanation: This is the correct statement about the reflection of light.

options.text: The angle of incidence is always opposite to the angle of reflection
options.explanation: This is not the correct statement about the reflection of light.

questions.explanation: The law of reflection states that the angle of incidence is always equal to the angle of reflection, which means that the angle at which light hits a surface is the same as the angle at which it bounces back.

questions.question: A person is looking at an object through a convex lens. If the object is moved closer to the lens, what happens to the image?

options.text: The image becomes smaller and closer to the lens
options.explanation: This is not the correct effect on the image.

options.text: The image becomes larger and closer to the lens
options.explanation: This is not the correct effect on the image.

options.text: The image becomes larger and farther away from the lens
options.explanation: This is the correct effect on the image.

options.text: The image becomes smaller and farther away from the lens
options.explanation: This is not the correct effect on the image.

questions.explanation: When an object is moved closer to a convex lens, the image becomes larger and farther away from the lens, because the lens is able to converge the light rays more effectively.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of total internal reflection?

options.text: Light passing from air into water
options.explanation: This is not an example of total internal reflection.

options.text: Light passing from water into air
options.explanation: This is not an example of total internal reflection.

options.text: Light passing from a denser medium into a rarer medium at a certain angle
options.explanation: This is an example of total internal reflection.

options.text: Light passing from a rarer medium into a denser medium
options.explanation: This is not an example of total internal reflection.

questions.explanation: Total internal reflection occurs when light passes from a denser medium into a rarer medium at a certain angle, known as the critical angle, and is completely reflected back into the denser medium.
